result.title: The Blindfolded Controller: Decision Model-Guided Training for Reinforcement Learning
result.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) provides a framework for continuous improvement through interaction with an environment. However, RL agents struggle against tasks that offer exploration challenges and sparse rewards, because learning efficient policies from scratch is slow and sample-inefficient. In contrast, decision models (DMs), given a description of the environment and task, can perform well in sparse-reward tasks, but, as they do not learn from reward, they are not able to improve towards the optimal solution. In this paper, we present Decision Model-Guided Training (DMGT), a technique that uses a DM with a description of the environment and task to initialise an RL policy, combining the DM's ability to act without training with RL's ability to improve from reward. Instead of exploring from scratch, the agent reaches the goal and receives reward from its first episodes, and RL then improves its policy beyond what the DM achieves. We demonstrate through experiments on seven tasks that our approach outperforms RL in all seven and DM in five. In addition, we provide comprehensive guidelines, derived from ablation studies, for describing an environment and task to a DM.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 DMGT：用决策模型（DM）依据环境与任务描述产生的行为来初始化强化学习策略，使智能体从最初几个回合即可获得奖励，再由 RL 继续改进并超越 DM，在七个稀疏奖励任务上验证并给出任务描述指南。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「先用任务描述条件化的外部模型提供初始策略、再用奖励信号继续校正」的结构，可能可供核查 LVR 中以教师轨迹初始化 latent 推理策略、再以结果奖励改进的训练安排；但该工作无视觉输入与推理期 latent 状态，迁移线索需较多核查。
